recommendations.text: Anaphylaxis is highly likely when any one of three clinical criteria is fulfilled, involving acute onset of skin/mucosal involvement plus respiratory compromise or reduced blood pressure.

For Anaphylaxis Recognition, the following actions are mandatory: - assess airway breathing circulation (within 2 minutes) - assess anaphylaxis criteria (within 3 minutes) - remove trigger if identifiable
During Anaphylaxis Recognition, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give antihistamine as first line, withhold epinephrine, give oral medication if vomiting.
Epinephrine (adrenaline) administered intramuscularly into the mid-outer thigh is the first-line treatment of anaphylaxis. There are no absolute contraindications to epinephrine in anaphylaxis.
For Epinephrine IM Administration, the following actions are mandatory: - give epinephrine im (within 5 minutes) - establish iv access (within 10 minutes) - position supine legs elevated

During Epinephrine IM Administration, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give epinephrine iv bolus, give epinephrine subcutaneous, give antihistamine as first line, withhold epinephrine, delay epinephrine for antihistamine, give sedative.
Beta-blocker patients may be resistant to epinephrine; glucagon bypasses beta-adrenergic blockade via direct cAMP stimulation. [REQUIRED: give_glucagon] (Severity: HIGH)

Beta-blocker patients may not respond to epinephrine; additional beta-blockade worsens anaphylactic shock. [FORBIDDEN: give_additional_beta_blocker_in_anaphylaxis, withhold_glucagon_despite_epi_resistance] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: WAO 2024 Section 4.3; EAACI 2024 Section 5.2; beta-blocker patients are epinephrine-resistant

recommendations.text: Pregnant patients must be positioned in left lateral decubitus to prevent aortocaval compression by the gravid uterus. [REQUIRED: position_left_lateral_decubitus] (Severity: HIGH)

Supine position in pregnant anaphylaxis causes aortocaval compression; methylergonovine is a vasoconstrictive contraindication. [FORBIDDEN: position_supine_flat_in_pregnancy, give_methylergonovine_in_anaphylaxis] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: WAO 2024 Section 6.1; supine positioning in pregnant patients causes aortocaval compression reducing cardiac output by 30%

recommendations.text: ACE inhibitors potentiate bradykinin-mediated angioedema; must never be readministered during anaphylaxis. [FORBIDDEN: give_ace_inhibitor_again, resume_ace_inhibitor] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Asthmatic patients have increased risk of severe bronchospasm during anaphylaxis; inhaled salbutamol is adjunctive to epinephrine. [REQUIRED: give_salbutamol_nebulized] (Severity: HIGH)

Beta-blockers worsen bronchospasm in asthmatic anaphylaxis; NSAIDs trigger aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease. [FORBIDDEN: give_beta_blocker_in_asthma_anaphylaxis, give_nsaid_in_aspirin_sensitive_asthma] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: WAO 2024 Section 4.5; beta-blockers exacerbate bronchospasm; NSAIDs trigger aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease

recommendations.text: Children under 12 must receive weight-based epinephrine dosing (0.01 mg/kg, max 0.3 mg); adult dose (0.5 mg) causes toxicity. [FORBIDDEN: give_adult_dose_epinephrine, give_epinephrine_0_5mg] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Normal saline 0.9% is recommended; 5-10 mL/kg in first 5-10 minutes for adults with hypotension. Up to 50 mL/kg may be required in first 30 minutes.
For Fluid Resuscitation, the following actions are mandatory: - give normal saline bolus (within 15 minutes) - reassess hemodynamic status (within 20 minutes)
During Fluid Resuscitation, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give epinephrine iv bolus, give colloid solution, withhold fluid in hypotension.
Mastocytosis patients have dramatically higher risk of protracted and biphasic anaphylaxis requiring extended observation. [REQUIRED: observe_minimum_24_hours] (Severity: HIGH)

Mastocytosis patients have dramatically higher biphasic reaction risk; NSAIDs trigger mast cell degranulation. [FORBIDDEN: discharge_before_24h_in_mastocytosis, give_nsaid_in_mastocytosis] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: WAO 2024 Section 6.3; Brockow K, JACI 2008; mastocytosis patients have 30% biphasic reaction rate

recommendations.text: Latex-allergic patients must be treated in a latex-free environment to prevent re-triggering anaphylaxis. [FORBIDDEN: use_latex_gloves_or_equipment, use_latex_containing_iv_tubing] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Upper airway angioedema may progress rapidly. Early intubation should be considered. Surgical airway may be needed if intubation fails due to severe edema.
For Airway Management, the following actions are mandatory: - reassess airway (within 15 minutes)
During Airway Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: give sedative, give benzodiazepine, discharge before airway stable.
All patients should be observed for a minimum of 4 hours. Patients with severe anaphylaxis, prior biphasic reactions, or mastocytosis require extended observation (8-24 hours).

For Monitoring and Disposition, the following actions are mandatory: - observe minimum 4 hours - prescribe epinephrine autoinjector (within 360 minutes) - provide anaphylaxis action plan (within 360 minutes) - refer to allergist

During Monitoring and Disposition, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: discharge before 4 hours, discharge without autoinjector prescription, discharge without action plan, discharge without allergist referral.
Patients with severe initial reactions have 10-20% risk of biphasic anaphylaxis occurring 1-72 hours after initial resolution. [REQUIRED: observe_minimum_8_hours] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: WAO 2024 Section 5.2; Grunau BE, Ann Emerg Med 2015

recommendations.text: Severe initial reactions have 10-20% biphasic risk; premature discharge or monitoring discontinuation is dangerous. [FORBIDDEN: discharge_before_8h_severe_anaphylaxis, discontinue_monitoring_prematurely] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: WAO 2024 Section 5.2; Grunau BE, Ann Emerg Med 2015; 10-20% biphasic rate in severe initial reactions
